verdict: No: the spec builds careful gates and error ids but gives a stranger no way to report a failure with usable evidence and no workable path to fix it, and the largest gap is that nothing produces or bounds what arrives in an issue while agents acting with the operator's account are the ones reading it.

findings.defect: No command or rule produces evidence a user can paste into an issue: error details are unspecified, there is no verbose or trace mode, and no output is declared safe to share.
findings.scenario: A stranger's `romeu run` fails inside sbxdrv after an sbx update; stderr shows `error RJ-1nn ...: <message>` and a fix hint, with no argv, no sbx stderr and no versions; `doctor --json` would add project names and keychain argv; the maintainer can only ask round after round or reproduce on their own Macs.
findings.change: In 04 4.1 Output, state that the details of a subprocess failure carry the escaped argv, exit status, the first N KiB of stderr and the romeu, julieta and sbx versions. In 04 4.2 add `romeu doctor --report` (or `romeu report`), which writes one redacted file: the versions of romeu, julieta, sbx, git and mise, macOS and arch, the doctor results and the last failing command's details, passed through the probe recorder's scrubber (10 10.3 Redaction). Add a rule to 05 that it prints no project name, path, secret argv or ledger field outside the closed sets, and a row to 00 0.5.
findings.cost: One command, one 04 4.1 paragraph, one 05 rule; reuses the recorder's redaction; one plan task.

findings.defect: The error table names no id for the failures field reports will be about, so most of them fall into a generic exit 1.
findings.scenario: sbx output no recorded parser accepts, a subprocess timeout, a registry fetch error or Docker Hub rate limit in sync step 6, a kit build failure inside `sbx env run`, each of the three compatibility-check causes (06 6.3) and each doctor check (04 4.2, J1 step 4) reach the user with no slug a maintainer can grep and no guide recovery.
findings.change: Add rows to the table of 04 4.1 by slug: sbx-output-unparsed, subprocess-timeout, registry-unreachable, kit-build-failed, julieta-protocol, julieta-digest, julieta-bin-writable, herdr-protocol; give each doctor check of 04 4.2 an id and a fix hint so the recovery per error id of 12 12.8 covers J1 step 4.
findings.cost: About ten table rows and their fixtures; a contracts approval.

findings.defect: The spec does not say what romeu does with an sbx version that no recording covers, once gate 1 is acknowledged.
findings.scenario: Docker ships sbx 0.48, the operator runs `romeu approve --toolchain` as 01 1.4 tells them, and sbxdrv's parsers, tuned to recorded versions (10 10.3 Parsers), misread a renamed field of `sbx ls --json`; identity (I26) or egress reconcile acts on a wrong reading instead of stopping with an id.
findings.change: In 01 1.4 state that gate 1 prints whether the live sbx version has a recording set, and that every sbx parse error exits 2 with sbx-output-unparsed naming the command and the recorded versions; in 10 10.3 state whether an unrecorded version runs with that warning or is refused.
findings.cost: One decision and two paragraphs.

findings.defect: 13 13.9 lists 'improving romeu and julieta ... (which error ids users hit)' as a consumer, but the ledger never leaves the machine and records no romeu failure, so the named consumer cannot read what it claims.
findings.scenario: A user's `romeu sync` fails repeatedly on gate 1 and in sbxdrv; nothing is recorded because romeu-side events are deferred (index: Deferred decisions, 'more event types and fields'), and the user's julieta events stay on the user's machine; the maintainer reads only their own ledger and concludes users hit nothing.
findings.change: Reword 13 13.9 to 'which error ids this machine hit', or reopen the deferred row now, since its trigger 'a consumer needs one' is met by 13 13.9's own row, adding a closed-field romeu-command-failed event (command, error id, exit, duration) that romeu writes into the ledger directly.
findings.cost: A wording change, or one event type with its generated tables.

findings.defect: Text from strangers on GitHub (issues, PR bodies, diffs) reaches agents acting with the operator's admin account, and no rule bounds what an agent may do with it; ADR 0008 names the class ('issue and PR text ... can steer the agent') and 05 has no row for it.
findings.scenario: A stranger opens an issue or a fork PR whose body tells a triaging agent to merge, re-run a workflow with secrets or edit a ruleset; the agent holds the operator's token (ADR 0008), so it takes effect; the token-narrowing trigger 'a second contributor' fires only after someone contributes, while the exposure starts with the first stranger's issue.
findings.change: Add a 05 5.4 row and a threat-model sentence in 05 for stranger text on GitHub; until the token is narrowed, state in 12 12.9 that agents read stranger issues and PRs as data only, take no merge, close, label or comment action on them in the operator's account without the maintainer's word, and mark any reply they write as an agent's; change the ADR 0008 trigger to 'the first issue or PR from an account other than the operator's'.
findings.cost: One residual-risk row, one working rule, one trigger change (an operator decision, an ADR 0008 follow-up record).

findings.defect: A stranger has no defined way to obtain the approval line every likely first PR needs: a catalog entry, an error id, a dependency bump or a check fix are all ask-first (05 5.3), and 07 7.5 step 2 itself sends users to 'a catalog PR'.
findings.scenario: A stranger follows the sync error and opens a catalog PR; `tools/ci pr` fails for the missing `Approval: catalog - "..."` line; the stranger cannot type the maintainer's words without inventing them, and docs/reference/ask-first.md does not say where to ask; the PR sits.
findings.change: In 12 12.4 state the stranger path: the author leaves the line out, `pr` names the surfaces that need it, and the maintainer adds the line as part of review (or comments it and the author pastes it verbatim); say the same in the generated ask-first page and the CONTRIBUTING outline of 12 12.8; in 07 7.6 state what a catalog PR's Evidence shows (the domains, how each upload flag was decided, the lock that names the tool).
findings.cost: Three paragraphs; message text in `pr`.

findings.defect: tools/ci has no failure-output contract like the RJ table, and several of its refusals cannot be diagnosed by a stranger: a forbidden-name hit reported by location only, an identity that holds a denylist substring, the exact-mise refusal, prose-rule hits in old commit messages.
findings.scenario: A stranger's PR goes red in `pr` with 'commit abc, field author: forbidden name' because their own name holds a hashed segment; nothing says what to do, and 10 10.2 calls it 'a cost of the check'; their local `fast` had already refused to run because their packaged mise is one version off.
findings.change: In 10 10.2 require every tools/ci failure line to carry the step, a rule id, the location and a fix line: for forbidden names 'reword this line; if it is your identity, ask the maintainer, who re-authors the commit'; for mise the exact version and the install command; for a prose hit in a commit message the rebase instruction.
findings.cost: A message table in tools/ci and one paragraph; matchers unchanged.

findings.defect: A merge gate whose result depends on the date (govulncheck in `all`) and the flake rule of 10 10.1 leave no owner for a red leg the change did not cause.
findings.scenario: An advisory for a dependency lands on a Tuesday and every open PR, the stranger's included, goes red in `vulnerabilities`; the stranger cannot fix go.mod (dependencies surface) and nothing says whether to wait, rebase or close.
findings.change: State in 10 10.2 that a red leg caused outside the change (an advisory, a flake, an upstream outage) is fixed on main first by the maintainer, the PR is rebased after, and CONTRIBUTING (12 12.8) says so.
findings.cost: Two sentences and a CONTRIBUTING line.

findings.defect: The bug classes most likely in the field are under 'Cannot model' with no test seam, so test-first (12 12.9, ADR 0003) cannot apply to their fixes, and a stranger cannot contribute the recording that would make such a bug testable.
findings.scenario: A stranger reports `run` hanging on sbx 0.48 during create; a fix needs a recording of that version (10 10.3 Floor bumps) and only block A, run by the maintainer, records; the fix waits for a sitting on both Macs and its PR has no failing test.
findings.change: In 10 10.3 accept a recording any user makes with the probe harness through the recorder's redaction, attached to an issue and committed by the maintainer after reading it; in 12 12.9 state that a fix for a Cannot-model class starts from a scenario replaying such a recording, or says under Evidence why none exists.

findings.defect: The spec defines what v1.0.0 needs and is silent on a patch release: whether a kit or catalog fix after v1.0.0 needs a candidate and block B again, and who cuts it.
findings.scenario: A stranger's catalog fix merges in March; nothing says whether v1.0.1 needs two Macs and about 90 minutes each (11 11.2) or ships on CI alone, so the fix waits indefinitely, or the v1.0.0 bar drops without anyone saying so.
findings.change: Add to 11 11.2 or 12 12.9 the post-v1 rule: which changed paths require block B (kits, sbxdrv, render), which ship on CI alone (catalog data, docs, error text), and that the maintainer tags.

findings.defect: Host state, render.json and host settings carry a version and strict decoding, but no rule says what a newer or older romeu does with them, so a rollback after a bad release becomes a decode failure on every command.
findings.scenario: A user upgrades to v1.1, which writes projects/<name>.json version 2, hits a regression and reinstalls v1.0; every command now exits 2 on an unknown version or key, with no id saying how to recover.
findings.change: In 03 3.4, 03 3.7 and 03 3.8 state a window like 03 3.6 and 13 13.7: romeu N reads N and N-1 and writes N, an older romeu refuses a newer record with a named id and a fix hint (reinstall the newer romeu), migrations are forward-only and atomic.
findings.cost: One paragraph per format and three error ids.

findings.defect: Issues have no usable shape: ADR 0001 and 12 12.7 give them the PR template and Conventional Commits, no check reads them (10 10.2), 02 2.1 has no issue templates, and bugs and PRs have no response expectation while SECURITY.md has one (12 12.8).
findings.scenario: A stranger opens 'it does not work' with no form asking for versions, command or output and no word on when anyone looks; three deferred triggers rely on a need 'written as an issue' (index: Deferred decisions), and those issues arrive without the facts a decision needs.
findings.change: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ (bug, catalog gap) to 02 2.1 with fields asking for the report file of L14-1; give issues their own row in ADR 0001's lead-practice table (a follow-up record); add to the 12 12.8 outlines a best-effort response expectation for issues and PRs and a README heading for when something goes wrong.
findings.cost: Two templates, an ADR change, outline lines; the README heading list is fixed before the candidate (11 11.2).

findings.defect: Release notes credit no contributor and link no issue, and the fix marker links a fix only to a release (12 12.10), so a reporter is never told their failure is fixed.
findings.scenario: A stranger's report is fixed in v1.0.2; the notes list `fix: ...` with the PR's Why; neither the reporter nor the stranger who fixed it is named and the issue stays open.
findings.change: In 12 12.6 have tools/release notes add each change's author handles and any `Fixes #<n>` reference, and add that convention next to `Fixes-release:` in 12 12.10.

findings.defect: No delivery number shows the stranger's experience, and maintainerWaitSeconds mixes agent PRs and outside PRs in one median.
findings.scenario: Agent PRs merge in an hour while outside PRs wait a month; the median still looks healthy, and the deferred merge-checkpoint decision (index: Deferred decisions) is read from a number that hides the wait that drives contributors away.
findings.change: In 12 12.10 report the maintainer wait and merged versus closed PRs split by whether the author is the operator's account, and the time to first response on issues, among the numbers that are not DORA's.

findings.defect: Only `romeu run` has `--timings`, and only as romeuMs and sbxMs; `sync`, `salvage`, `rm` and `retire`, which cross many steps and two machines, have no per-step timing or trace, so a maintainer cannot see in which step the time or the failure went.
findings.scenario: A user reports that `romeu rm` takes ten minutes then exits 5; nothing shows whether ingest, `julieta salvage`, bundle verify or the daemon fetch took the time, or which step produced the skipped item.
findings.change: Generalize `--timings [--json]` in 04 4.1 to every mutating romeu command, with one entry per numbered step of 04 4.2 (sync 1-10, run 1-8, the two salvage halves) and the sbx and git subprocess time inside each, and include it in the report of L14-1.

findings.defect: The ARCHITECTURE.md outline gives no read-first path per critical flow, and nothing checks that each error id leads to a recovery (plan.md T094 marks it [review]; ADR 0001 rule 16 is review-only).

findings.defect: The field failure modes of a host tool with no server (a full disk during sync, salvage or a bundle write; a mount permission change; egress denied at runtime) have no error id, doctor check or runbook, apart from the ledger temporary file (13 13.10).

postmortem:
# Postmortem: romeu e julieta, after v1.0.0

Written by the maintainer on duty, as I would see it fail. One page.

**What happened.** v1.0.0 shipped clean: S1-S11 green, block B passed on
both Macs. Over the next months a dozen strangers tried it. Three opened
issues, one sent a PR. None came back. The project became what its spec
describes: one developer and their agents.

**Why, in the order it hurt.**

1. **Docker moved and we could not see where.** sbx updated, gate 1
   exited 3 everywhere (01 1.4), people ran `approve --toolchain`, and the
   parsers tuned to recorded versions met an unrecorded one (04 4.2 step
   4, 10 10.3 "Floor bumps"). The report said "run fails, RJ-1xx". The
   error had no argv, no sbx stderr, no versions (04 4.1 Output). We
   could only reproduce on the maintainer's Macs, at the next sitting.
2. **Nobody could send us a report we could use.** There is no issue
   form (02 2.1), no diagnostic command (04 4.2, 4.3), no rule for what
   is safe to paste from `doctor`, `status` or `ledger query` (all print
   project names and keychain argv). Issues were held to the PR template
   (12 12.7, ADR 0001), which fits a report not at all. The ledger, built
   "for improving romeu" (13 13.9, ADR 0006), never left the reporter's
   machine and records nothing romeu itself does (13 13.2).
3. **The obvious first PR was the most gated.** `sync` told the user to
   send "a catalog PR" (07 7.5 step 2). The catalog is ask-first
   (05 5.3), so is the error table (`contracts`), so is every check
   (`checks`). The stranger needed an approval line of "the maintainer's
   words" (12 12.4) and no page said how to get them. The PR sat.
4. **CI was red for reasons outside the change.** `govulncheck` is date
   dependent and in `all` (10 10.2); a flake had no named owner (10 10.1);
   the stranger's own name could trip the hashed denylist, reported by
   location only (10 10.2, Forbidden names). The local run refused their
   mise version before checking anything (10 10.2). The failure output of
   `tools/ci` had no contract like the RJ table. They closed the PR.
5. **The fix could not be tested where the bug lived.** The bugs that
   matter are in "Cannot model": VM boot, virtiofs, kit builds, network
   policy, credential injection (10 10.3). Test-first (12 12.9, ADR 0003)
   had no seam for them; host and probe levels are "maintainer machines"
   (10 10.1, 11). A stranger's redacted recording was never invited.
6. **Even a merged fix reached nobody quickly.** 11 11.2 ties a kit or
   catalog fix to a new candidate and block B; nothing said what v1.0.1
   needs. Fixes waited for a sitting with two Macs. Release notes did not
   name the contributor or the issue (12 12.6, 12 12.10 fix marker links to
   a release, not an issue). Docs on `main` described flags the reporter's
   binary did not have (Deferred: docs versioning).
7. **The thing I would not say out loud: an agent answered them.** The
   sandbox acts as the maintainer on GitHub (ADR 0008, 05 5.4). Agents
   triaged, labelled and reviewed stranger issues and PRs in the
   maintainer's account. ADR 0008 itself lists "issue and PR text ... can
   steer the agent", and no rule followed (05 threat model, 5.4). One
   crafted issue was enough to make an agent with admin rights act on it;
   the polite strangers just felt they were talking to a bot that never
   said so.
8. **No number told us.** `tools/ci dora` measured merges and releases
   (12 12.10, ADR 0004); `maintainerWaitSeconds` mixed agent PRs and
   stranger PRs. No metric of time to first response or of stranger PRs
   merged. The deferred triggers that strangers fire ("a second
   contributor", "first PR from outside", "written as an issue") were
   watched by review rounds that ended with v1 (ADR 0005 Consequences,
   index Deferred decisions).

**Root cause.** The spec's reader is "the planner and implementers of
v1, and reviewers of the design" (index). Its newcomer is a contributor
who scaffolds (index, Simple and explicit). The stranger who reports and
the stranger who fixes are not users of this spec, so v1 had no door for
either, and every gate built for an agent with the operator's token
landed on them instead.
lens_critique: The lens judges success by strangers who report, fix and come back, but v1 is declared to serve one developer with no support promise (00 0.2), so part of what the lens asks for (response targets, contributor metrics, triage) is a cost the spec could rightly defer with triggers rather than build now. It also undervalues that the first field reports are the maintainer's own, on two Macs, and that the same diagnostic machinery serves them first; and it pulls toward verbose free-text logs, which collide with the no-free-text rule of 13, where closed-field, redacted evidence is the better answer.
missing_viewpoint: The upstream partner: someone who reads the spec as the vendors of the sandbox runtime and of the agent would, to ask which unstable behaviours of the sandbox tool, the kit frontend and the agent the product leans on, and what channel back to those upstreams exists when one of them changes.

out_of_scope.why: the text alone cannot settle it; ledgers of real size from the field would

out_of_scope.what: cryptographic soundness of the gates, digests and signing rule
out_of_scope.why: this person would not look at it; L2 and L7 own it

out_of_scope.what: whether the sbx behaviours block A records are stable
out_of_scope.why: the text alone cannot settle it; the block A results and later sbx releases would

out_of_scope.what: the plan's order and size beyond the parked notes
out_of_scope.why: this person would not look at it; L9 owns it

confidence: High that each gap exists (each checked against the cited text); medium on severities, since the one-developer scope of v1 makes some of them deferrable.
